items.abstract: <jats:p>Scientific AI systems are increasingly expected to reason over scarce observations, noisy measurements, unstable simulators, and heterogeneous model families. Existing work usually treats these difficulties separately: robust surrogate models address noisy regression, routing systems select among language models, and control-theoretic allocation methods adapt traffic under non-stationary workloads. This paper argues that noisy, data-scarce scientific workflows require an integrated agent architecture rather than a single fixed predictor. We introduce Robust Scientific AI Agents (RSA-Agents), a framework that represents scientific problem solving as a closed-loop decision process over candidate surrogate models, symbolic tools, validation signals, uncertainty estimates, and execution constraints. The agent maintains a portfolio of candidate scientific models, estimates their task-conditioned reliability from limited evidence, and allocates future calls through a validation-weighted selection rule with persistent exploration. Noise-robust models such as ER-KAN provide the agent with a safer surrogate option when clean-data accuracy is misleading, while adaptive routing and feedback-control principles prevent static model commitments under regime change. In a synthetic pilot benchmark spanning eight analytic functions, three data budgets, and three noise levels, a validation-weighted RSA-Agent reduces mean squared error by 7.7% relative to the best static surrogate overall and by 27.7% in the high-noise setting, while underperforming on clean regimes. These results support the central thesis: robust scientific AI should be evaluated as an adaptive agentic system under uncertainty, not only as a collection of isolated predictors.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Recent developments in large language models allow for real time, context-aware tutoring. AI Gem, presented in this article, is a layered architecture that integrates personalization, adaptive feedback, and curricular alignment into transformer based tutoring agents. The architecture combines retrieval augmented generation, Bayesian learner model, and policy-based dialog in a verifiable and deployable software stack. The opportunities are scalable tutoring, multimodal interaction, and augmentation of teachers through content tools and analytics. Risks are factual errors, bias, over reliance, latency, cost, and privacy. The paper positions AI Gem as a design framework with testable hypotheses. A scenario-based walkthrough and new diagrams assign each learner step to the ten layers. Governance guidance covers data privacy across jurisdictions and operation in resource constrained environments.</jats:p>
title: AI Gem: Context-Aware Transformer Agents as Digital Twin Tutors for Adaptive Learning
